text: "And Sulaiman inherited Dawud." Prophet Sulaiman, alayhis salaam, became prophet and king after his father.
And he made a dua: "My Lord, forgive me, and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
He asked for forgiveness first. Then for the kingdom.
And Allah answered. "So We subjected to him the wind, blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed."
A morning's journey on that wind was a month's travel. An evening's journey was another month.
And Allah made a spring of molten copper flow for him, and the jinn worked for him by his Lord's permission: high palaces, great bowls like reservoirs, cooking pots fixed to the ground.
But with all of it came one command: "Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude. And few of My servants are grateful."
Few are grateful. Would Prophet Sulaiman, alayhis salaam, be one of the few?
